section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: Rainfall caused by warm, moist air rising over a mountain range, cooling and condensing as it ascends, is called:
explanation: Orographic rainfall occurs when moist air is forced upward by a mountain barrier, cooling and condensing — a major rainfall type on the windward side of the Western Ghats.

section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: India follows a single standard time zone based on the meridian passing through:

options.option_text: 82.5° E longitude, near Mirzapur (Indian Standard Time)

explanation: Indian Standard Time (IST) is based on 82.5° E longitude, passing near Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh), giving a single time zone despite India's east-west span.

section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Nile, the longest river in the world (by traditional measurement), flows through which continent?
explanation: The Nile flows through north-eastern Africa, emptying into the Mediterranean Sea. The Amazon (South America) is the largest by volume/basin size.

section: Social Studies · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Himalayas were formed primarily due to:

options.option_text: The collision of the Indian tectonic plate with the Eurasian plate
Volcanic eruptions building up layer by layer
Wind erosion carving out peaks over millions of years

explanation: The Himalayas are fold mountains formed by the ongoing collision of the Indian Plate with the Eurasian Plate, which is why the range is still slowly rising today.
